clue.text: Nobody else could have created this work of art

definitions.text: Nobody else could have created this work of art

parts.words: Nobody else could have created this work of art
parts.note: a picture of the artist by the artist: no other painter could make it, since its subject is the maker

explanation.definitionFit: A painting an artist makes of their own face and figure is a work only that artist can produce.

clue.text: Successfully putting evil monarch here

parts.note: evil as a noun is wickedness, a sin
a monarch such as a king

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having put a wicked ruler in his place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' looks like placing, but it is the golf stroke: the def is about holing the ball. 'here' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, holing a putt is called sinking it.

clue.text: Was Dickens upwardly mobile?

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word moving upwards is read from the bottom, so the letters come out backwards

parts.note: 'the dickens' is an old euphemism for the devil, as in 'what the dickens'

explanation.surface: A question about whether the novelist Charles Dickens climbed the social ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens is not the novelist but the old oath 'what the dickens', meaning the devil; DEVIL written upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have existed or been alive is to have had life, so 'was' and the answer both mean existed.

clue.text: People of a certain age look right in work at university

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the word for work and the university phrase

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does
UP means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A description of students of the same age studying together at university.
explanation.walkthrough: UP for 'at university' is a British convention: students are said to be up at Oxford or Cambridge. 'in' places the right letter after the first letter of the work word.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer group is the set of people of similar age and status one mixes with.

clue.text: Give another performance in theatre, then dine

parts.note: REP is short for repertory theatre
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: An actor appears on stage and then goes out for supper.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform something again is to do it once more, a second showing.

clue.text: Revolutionary movement helping to trap old tyrant, finally

indicators.note: one piece catches the others inside it, as a trap holds its prey

parts.note: a helping is a portion, a ration

indicators.note: says to take only the closing letter of the word tyrant

explanation.surface: A political uprising is helping to capture an ageing dictator at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics, but here it means turning round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning about an axis is a revolving motion, so a revolution in the physical sense.

clue.text: Irish politicians I sent up in classic work

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending both pieces upwards writes the whole run backwards

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: Irish politicians make fun of a famous old poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns DAILI into the answer; it also suggests mockery in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem of the Trojan War is a classical masterpiece of Greek literature.

clue.text: Firm needing a line to Shanghai, say, in China

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
Shanghai is an example of a port

explanation.surface: A business needs a shipping route to a big port in the People's Republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' at the end looks like the country next to Shanghai, but it is porcelain; capital letters can mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Coalport is a famous English make of porcelain tableware from Shropshire.

clue.text: Occupied with change of course in storm

parts.note: to be at something is to be busy with it, as in 'hard at work'
a sailing boat tacks when it changes its course into the wind

explanation.surface: A sailor busy altering direction in rough weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' looks like weather, completing the sailing picture, but it is a verb: to storm a fort.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to assault it forcefully.

clue.text: English county once turned to stars of variable brilliance

indicators.note: the county's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Avon was an English county from 1974 to 1996

explanation.surface: A former English county has changed into a place of shimmering stars.
explanation.definitionFit: These are stars that flare up suddenly to great brightness and then fade.

clue.text: Cape secured by tie at 'top, changed for another garment

indicators.note: one piece is held fast inside the other, as if fastened by it
says the letters of tie at top are put in a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: A cape fastened at the neck with a tie is swapped for a different item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges TIEATTOP; 'secured by' puts C inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A petticoat is a woman's light underskirt, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Asian's good name concealed time to get angry

indicators.note: the Asian word hides two letters within it

parts.note: an Indian is an Asian person

explanation.surface: An Asian man's reputation was hidden, giving him reason to lose his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Indignant means aggrieved and resentful at perceived unfair treatment.

clue.text: Daedalus started with this sort of wing

definitions.meaning: Daedalus begins with the letter D, which is called this in the radio alphabet
a triangular swept-back aircraft wing is named after the Greek letter

explanation.walkthrough: Daedalus made wings in Greek myth, so 'started with' looks like a story about his flying, but it means his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The NATO code word for D, and the triangular wing shape named from the Greek letter.

clue.text: Writer' whose work Waugh abridged

parts.note: Evelyn Waugh's novel Decline and Fall shortens the title of an eighteenth-century history, Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire

explanation.walkthrough: 'abridged' suggests Waugh edited the book, but he only borrowed a shortened form of its title.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Gibbon wrote The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire; Waugh's novel title cuts it short.

clue.text: Supports British criminal activity

parts.note: rackets are criminal money-making schemes

explanation.surface: Someone endorses organised crime in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall brackets are fixtures that hold up shelves, so they are supports.

clue.text: It's bound to include a lot of numbers

definitions.text: It's bound to include a lot of numbers

parts.words: It's bound to include a lot of numbers
parts.note: reads like a certainty about statistics, but 'bound' means bookbound and 'numbers' means musical pieces

explanation.definitionFit: A bound collection of songs, each one a musical number.

clue.text: Person in trial given money to eat a lot

parts.note: a guinea is an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings
to pig, or pig out, is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A volunteer in a study is paid to stuff themselves with food.
explanation.definitionFit: A test subject used in an experiment is commonly called this, after the laboratory rodent.

clue.text: Group of soldiers, none the less, in charge of old philosopher

indicators.note: says the word for nothing is taken away from the soldiers' unit

parts.note: a platoon is a small unit of soldiers
O, the figure nought, stands for none

explanation.surface: A unit of troops, though no smaller, is commanded by an ancient thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'none the less' looks like 'nevertheless', but means less an O (nought) from PLATOON, leaving PLATON.
explanation.definitionFit: Platonic means relating to Plato, the ancient Greek philosopher.

clue.text: Decline European as standard-bearer

parts.note: to flag is to tire or decline
a Pole is a European

explanation.surface: A declining European is chosen to carry the banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and the tall staff it flies from bears it.

clue.text: Condition lifted, since company is a total failure

indicators.note: in a down clue, a lifted word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: if introduces a condition
as can mean since, because

explanation.surface: Once restrictions are raised, the firm collapses completely.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating complete disaster.

clue.text: Tent needed by Mae West, for one?

definitions.meaning: the big canvas tent of a circus

definitions.text: needed by Mae West, for one?
definitions.meaning: the actress Mae West was famously buxom, so would need a large upper garment

explanation.definitionFit: The main circus tent; read as two words, a large top for a big bust.

clue.text: Protection for cricketer cut in the field

parts.note: a batsman in cricket wears a pad on each leg
to dock a tail is to cut it short

explanation.surface: A cricketer's leg guard is trimmed down while out fielding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the field' sounds like a cricketer fielding, but 'field' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddock is a small enclosed field for horses.

clue.text: Fruit top-class, I found, in holiday islands

parts.note: the haw is the berry of the hawthorn
A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: First-rate fruit discovered on a tropical getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written as AI, the digit 1 standing for I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific US state is an island group popular with tourists.

clue.text: Oblique request to opposites S — will they never meet?

parts.note: to request is to ask
East and West are opposite compass points, abbreviated E and W

explanation.surface: An indirect plea to two people who can never get together.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail echoes Kipling's 'East is East, and West is West, and never the twain shall meet', pointing to E and W.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew is crooked or at a slant, not straight.

clue.text: So called rabbit isn't from neighbouring land

definitions.text: So called rabbit isn't from neighbouring land

parts.words: So called rabbit isn't from neighbouring land
parts.note: the cheese-on-toast dish called rabbit contains no rabbit, and is named for a nation bordering England

explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is not the animal but the old dish name; the clue says the name is false.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rabbit (rarebit) is cheese on toast; the adjective names Wales, England's neighbour.

clue.text: Came across part of song in jazz style

indicators.note: the song part is placed inside the jazz word

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz
a verse is a section of a song

explanation.surface: Someone discovered a stanza written in a jazz idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to cross over, so came across means went across here.

clue.text: American tucked into his cooked Oriental food

indicators.note: one piece is slipped inside the other
cooking alters, so the letters of his are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American eats his prepared Japanese meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his cooked' sounds like a chef preparing the meal, but 'cooked' only signals rearranging those three letters before the American abbreviation goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish.

clue.text: Look into Italian port or part of Spain

indicators.note: the word for look goes inside the port's name

parts.note: Catania is a port in Sicily
lo is an old word meaning look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: A traveller inspects an Italian harbour or a Spanish region.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalonia is an autonomous region in north-east Spain.

clue.text: Bother with duck sauce

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance or bother
in cricket a duck is a score of zero, written O

explanation.surface: Someone is fussing over the sauce for a duck dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' suggests the bird with a sauce, but it is a cricket score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts and cheese.

clue.text: Counterpart of electric blue for girl?

definitions.text: Counterpart of electric blue for girl?

parts.words: Counterpart of electric blue for girl?
parts.note: blue is the traditional colour for boys and pink for girls, so a vivid blue pairs with a vivid pink

explanation.definitionFit: A vivid bright pink, the girls' match to a vivid bright blue.
